summary: Turns the search page into a client component that reads q from the URL. It fetches matching products and renders them as a list.

findings.title: URL query rendered as raw HTML
findings.description: The heading puts the q URL parameter into dangerouslySetInnerHTML without escaping. The query text therefore reaches the DOM as live HTML. An attacker can send a link such as /search?q= to run script in the victim's session. This is reflected XSS. Render the query as a normal JSX text child so that React escapes it.

findings.consequence: An attacker can send a link such as /search?q= to run script in the victim's session. This is reflected XSS.
findings.fix: Render the query as a normal JSX text child so that React escapes it.

findings.title: Effect without dependencies refetches forever
findings.description: The useEffect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render. Each run calls setResults with a new array, which causes another render. The page sends an endless stream of requests to /api/products. This loads the API and keeps re-rendering the browser tab. Pass [query] as the dependency array so that the page fetches only when the query changes.

findings.title: Hooks called after a conditional return
findings.description: SearchPage returns early when q is empty, before it calls useState and useEffect. The number of hooks therefore changes between renders. React throws a rendered-more-hooks error when q goes from empty to set during client navigation. The page then crashes. Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Inside the effect, skip the fetch when query is empty.
findings.problem: SearchPage returns early when q is empty, before it calls useState and useEffect. The number of hooks therefore changes between renders.
findings.consequence: React throws a rendered-more-hooks error when q goes from empty to set during client navigation. The page then crashes.
findings.fix: Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Inside the effect, skip the fetch when query is empty.

findings.title: Search request rejection is unhandled
findings.description: The effect chains .then on searchProducts but never adds a .catch. searchProducts throws when the response is not ok. A failed search produces an unhandled promise rejection. The user sees stale or empty results with no error message. Add a .catch handler that records an error state and shows the error to the user.

findings.consequence: A failed search produces an unhandled promise rejection. The user sees stale or empty results with no error message.
findings.fix: Add a .catch handler that records an error state and shows the error to the user.

findings.title: List items rendered without a key
findings.description: The results map renders each li without a key prop. Product already has a stable id field. React cannot match list items correctly when the results change. It also logs a key warning. Set key to product.id on each li.
findings.problem: The results map renders each li without a key prop. Product already has a stable id field.
findings.consequence: React cannot match list items correctly when the results change. It also logs a key warning.
findings.fix: Set key to product.id on each li.

findings.title: Search form removed with no replacement
findings.description: The change deletes the search form, and no other file in the repository renders an input named q. The empty state still tells users to type a search term. Users have no input to type into. They can search only by editing the URL by hand. Keep the form with the q input on the page, alongside the results list.
